newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Stock Exchange net surplus falls.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Stock Exchange net surplus falls.

text.p: The Australian Stock Exchange (ASX) said on Tuesday its net operating surplus fell to A$11.54 million in the first half of the 1996/97 year (July-June) from A$11.89 million a year ago.
The ASX, whose members agreed to demutualise last October, said its first half net surplus was a substantial improvement on the A$7.49 million achieved in the 1995/96 second half.
Total revenue rose to A$62.61 million from A$57.08 million a year ago and from A$56.80 million in the 1995/96 second half.
The ASX said it ranked as the tenth largest equities market in the world at the end of December 1996, based on data from the International Federation of Stock Exchanges.
Equities market turnover exceeded A$100 billion for the first time in the latest six months, a rise of 36 percent on year-ago levels and a 17 percent increase on the 1995/96 second half.

The benchmark All Ordinaries index rose 8.1 percent in the latest period to end the calendar year at a record high of 2424.6 points and earnings yields were 5.2 percent higher than a year ago but down a full percentage point on July 1996.

The ASX said activity on the derivatives market continued to grow, with 5.5 million contracts traded representing a rise of five percent on the 1995/96 second half and a 20 percent increase on the year-ago level.

It said there was a 20 percent rise in Low Exercise Price Options (LEPO) contracts compared with the 1995/96 second half and open interest in LEPOs at the end of December was three times higher than that in the competing product on the Sydney Futures Exchange.
